condition.narrative: Financing Agreement. Schedule 2 Section I.A. 4(b) The Recipient shall not later than three (3) months after the Effective date,recruit a dedicated Project accountant, procurement specialist, monitoring and evaluation specialist, environmental specialist,social development specialist, public health specialist, and communication specialist for the Project Implementation Unit, underterms of reference and with qualification and experience acceptable to the Association.

Financing Agreement. Schedule 2 Section I.A. 4(c) The Recipient shall not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date,recruit or second an internal auditor for the Project Implementation Unit, under terms of reference and with qualification andexperience acceptable to the Association.

Financing Agreement. Schedule 2 Section III B.2 The Recipient undertakes that no Financing and/or GFF Grant proceeds or resourcesmay be used for law-enforcement, security, military, or paramilitary purposes or for any payments made to any law-enforcement,security, military, or paramilitary forces without the express approval of the Association (acting on its own behalf or asadministrator of the GFF Grant funds).

Financing Agreement. Schedule 2, Section I.A. 4(a) The Recipient shall not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date,recruit a Project manager to lead the implementation of Project activities, under terms of reference and with qualifications andexperience acceptable to the Association, and to coordinate with the directorate of finance, directorate of internal audit, theprocurement unit and other technical directorates within the Ministry of Health on Project implementation and adherence tofiduciary guidelines.

The Recipient shall maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, a project implementation unit in the Ministryof Health (“Sub-PIU”) with a mandate, terms of reference, composition, and resources satisfactory to the Association and to thisend the Recipient shall no later than one (1) months after the Effective Date recruit a financial management specialist and assign(second) to Sub-PIU, a Sub-PIU coordinator, an immunization expert, a cold chain and logistics officer, a monitoring and evaluationofficer and an RMNCAH-N specialist, all under terms of reference and with qualifications and experience acceptable to theAssociation.

The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association on an annual basis, by no later than October 31 of each year, commencingon October 31, 2021, the annual work plan and budget containing all activities proposed to be included in the Project during thefollowing Fiscal Year, and a proposed financing plan (setting forth the proposed amounts and sources of financing for expendituresrequired for such activities

title.narrative: Number of health workers trained in COVID-19 case management [by gender]
Percentage of designated hospitals with functional oxygen delivery equipment

comment.narrative: The project procured oxygen cylinders, oxygen regulators, venture masks, nasal cannulas, Guedels airway, intubation sets, tubing, highflow delivery masks, flowmeters, non-rebreather masks. The project is also procuring 15 mobile PSA oxygen plants to be stationed in health facilities that will be used as regional hubs to supply oxygen through filling of cylinders for periphery health facilities in addition to piping oxygen to the hospital where the plant will be sited.

title.narrative: Number of health workers trained in COVID-19 case management [by gender]

comment.narrative: Cumulatively 3,096 (1,546M/1,550F) health workers have been trained in Covid-19 case management mental health and psychosocial support. In 2024, 645 health workers were trained as Trainer of Trainers (TOTs) and these subsequently trained about 3,175. The COVID-19 treatment guidelines that were developed through project support were also used by other institutions to train additional health staff (Project Reports).

title.narrative: Percentage of designated hospitals with functional oxygen delivery equipment

comment.narrative: The project procured and installed 15 modular pressure swing adsorption mobile mini oxygen plants with a capacity of 30m3 for national and provincial COVID-19 treatment centres with selected district hospitals established as regional distribution hubs for filled oxygen cylinders for nearby facilities. The oxygen plants are also able to pipe oxygen to the hospitals where they are sited. The project also procured oxygen cylinders, oxygen regulators, ventura masks, nasal cannulas, airway guedels, intubation sets, tubing, high-flow delivery masks, flowmeters, non-rebreather masks, etc. (Project reports)

title.narrative: Percentage of designated health facilities with an improved water source on premises

comment.narrative: project will support drilling of 20 water sources at health facilitates which have already been identified/approved by MOH. The project has completed E&S screening of the selected sites.

title.narrative: Percentage of designated health facilities with an improved water source on premises

comment.narrative: The Project could not support the drilling of 20 water sources at health facilitates because of limited time before closure; hence the procurement process was cancelled. However, Project procured 25 x 10,000 litre capacity water storage tanks and 200 (each with a 500 litre water tank) permanent hand washing facilities to improve the water source for WASH. (Project Reports).

title.narrative: Number of dedicated quarantine and isolation centers

comment.narrative: Out of the 120 isolation centers in all the districts, 80 have been supported by the Project with medical equipment, PPEs and disinfectants.

title.narrative: Number of dedicated quarantine and isolation centers

comment.narrative: The project has support 144 quarantine and isolation centers in all the districts with medical equipment, PPEs and disinfectants.

title.narrative: Number of designated laboratories with SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic capacity (Number)

comment.narrative: currently supported by the Government of Zambia, Development Partners and the private sector. The Project has supported 17 laboratories with reagents and consumables and procured and distributed PCR test kits and reagents, rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) 22 public laboratories conducting PCR testing and all those health facilities offering RDTs.

title.narrative: Number of designated laboratories with SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic capacity (Number)

comment.narrative: The Project procured laboratory equipment, PCR test kits and reagent, and rapid diagnostic test kits (RDTs) that were distributed to the 25 public laboratories and all health facilities offering rapid diagnostic testing

title.narrative: Number of designated health facilities with COVID-19 case management capacity

comment.narrative: Target reduced in the December 2023 project restructuring from 50to 25. The Project procured and delivered various equipment: such as 400 patient monitors, 200 suction pumps, 100 infusion pumps, 1000 laryngoscopes, 10 digital X-ray machines for more than 100 COVID-19 treatment centers and health facilities and has committed to installing 15 oxygen plants.

title.narrative: Number of designated health facilities with COVID-19 case management capacity

comment.narrative: The Project procured and installed 15 oxygen plants in national and provincial COVID-19 treatment centres, and 10 digital x-ray machines. The Project also procured and distributed high-flow oxygen delivery equipment, 400 patient monitors, 100 suction pumps and 200 infusion pumps, 1,000 laryngoscopes, PEPs, etc. and has distributed the supplies to about 144 COVID-19 isolation / quarantine / treatment centers

comment.narrative: project has procured 30 Ultrasound machines supporting capacity building of staff in essential and advanced newborn care. Project is also committed to finance telemedicine pilot and procurement of equipment for specialized neonatal units (DHIS2)

title.narrative: Monthly average number of deliveries attended by skilled personnel

comment.narrative: Project supported capacity building of staff in essential newborn care and advanced newborn care. Project also supported a telemedicine pilot and procurement of ultrasound and specialized neonatal Ambulance units (DHIS2)

title.narrative: Number of Health Facilities equipped with energy efficient storage facilities for vaccines and temperature sensitive medical supplies

comment.narrative: Procurement of cold chain equipment and spare parts is included in the 2024 Procurement Plan and the procurement process has been initiated. (Project Reports)

title.narrative: Number of operational research studies conducted to inform the national COVID-19 response

comment.narrative: 3 operational research activities have been agreed upon and the study protocol for the COVID 19 home based care research has been approved by the UNZABREC.Training of enumerators and supervisors was done in December 2023. Field work was delayed due to the cholera outbreak (Project Reports)

title.narrative: Number of Health Facilities equipped with energy efficient storage facilities for vaccines and temperature sensitive medical supplies

comment.narrative: The procurement and delivery of cold chain equipment such as solar fridges, cool boxes, spares for the repair of faulty equipment and a 15-ton refrigerated truck increased the number of health facilities with energy efficient storage facilities across the referral system; with most clinics acting as cold chain storage hubs for other health facilities within their vicinity (Project Reports).

title.narrative: Number of operational research studies conducted to inform the national COVID-19 response

comment.narrative: Two operational research studies were completed: namely 1) COVID-19 home-based care management in Zambia and 2) Characterization of Long COVID-19 and Long-Term Sequelae in Zambia after 144 weeks of the COVID-19 Pandemic (Project Reports)

title.narrative: Number of designated laboratories with capacity for genomic sequencing

comment.narrative: 1) ZNPHRL, 2) UNZA VET, 3) Macha Research Trust, 4) CHAZ and 5) TDRC (ZNPHI LSN). The Project procured some genomic sequencing laboratory supplies and trained key staff from the five laboratories in the genomic sequencing process that included biostatical informatics.

title.narrative: Number of designated laboratories with capacity for genomic sequencing

comment.narrative: There are currently 6 laboratories in the country providing genomic sequencing supported by the Government, development partners and the private sector (1. ZNPHRL 2. UNZA Vet 3. Macha Research Trust 4. Churches Health Association of Zambia - CHAZ 5. Tropical Diseases Research Centre TDRC (ZNPHI Reports). The project is committed to procuring genomic sequencing reagents and train laboratory personnel to enhance the capacity of 5 public laboratories.

title.narrative: Number of health workers who are fully vaccinated against COVID-19 [by gender]

comment.narrative: 37,476 males; 46,911 females health workers have been vaccinated. The data is not disaggregated according to profession. Currently, the data sources include accountants, auditors in the definition of health workers - the M and E system needs to be strengthened to obtain more accurate data.

title.narrative: Number of health workers who are fully vaccinated against COVID-19 [by gender]

comment.narrative: 38,101 male and 47,861 female health workers were vaccinated. The data doesn’t segregate according to profession within the health sector (DHIS2 – Covax Tracker).

title.narrative: Key messages and materials developed for public communications and advocacy, in alignment with demand plan, and establishing two-way feedback and response mechanisms

comment.narrative: The project continues to support RCCE message development (Project Reports)

title.narrative: Key messages and materials developed for public communications and advocacy, in alignment with demand plan, and establishing two-way feedback and response mechanisms

comment.narrative: The project supported Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) message development as part of the national, provincial and district micro-plans for December 2021 Vaccination Campaign. there is an on-going assessment to establish the two way mechanism to close the feedback loop.

title.narrative: DHIS2 COVID-19 Vaccine delivery Tool Kit implemented (YES/No)

comment.narrative: Training of staff on the use of DHIS2 COVID 19 Vaccine Delivery Tool Kit planned for the end of Q2 2024 (Project Reports).

title.narrative: DHIS2 COVID-19 Vaccine delivery Tool Kit implemented (YES/No)

comment.narrative: Training of staff on use of DHIS2 COVID-19 vaccine delivery toolkit was not undertaken. However, the MOH with support from other partners such as WHO and Global Fund enabled the MOH/ZNPHI to commence the development and operationalizing a web-based Vaccine Logistics System on open Source eLMIS platform (Project Reports)

title.narrative: Proportion of eligible population fully vaccinated, which is included in the priority targets defined in the National Plan (by gender)

comment.narrative: Fully vaccinated 3,929,474 males and 4,863,257 females, exceeding 70% COVID -19 vaccination benchmark set by WHO (DHIS2 - Covax Tracker)

title.narrative: Proportion of eligible population fully vaccinated, which is included in the priority targets defined in the National Plan (by gender)

comment.narrative: Fully vaccinated 4,283,196 males and 5,304,198 females. At 94%, the revised project target of 90% and national target of 70% COVID-19 vaccination benchmark set by WHO for countries to attain head immunity were surpassed (DHIS2 – Covax Tracker)

title.narrative: Number of fully equipped provincial blood storage hubs established and operational in compliance with national standards

comment.narrative: Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) for the 6 sites have been developed

title.narrative: Number of fully equipped provincial blood storage hubs established and operational in compliance with national standards

comment.narrative: Although Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) for the 6 sites were developed; due to limited time before closure, the project instead focused on procuring cold chain equipment to facilitate the establishment and functionality of 20 provincial blood storage hubs. Equipment was installed and commissioned in 2024. The targeted health facilities provided space to house the blood storage hubs. The cold chain equipment, together with the supply of motor vehicles and cool boxes greatly improved the transportation and storage processed blood at these facilities including the last mile distribution.
